notes.title: Landlord s Super is a sim about work, poverty, and booze, and it's coming to early access this month
notes.notes:
There’s only one class to choose in Landlord’s Super: working class. Set in a Midlands town in the ‘80s (a famously prosperous time in the UK when no contentious things happened), it’s a game about the ordinary feats of strength people do to get by. Trading in scrap for cash, finding odd jobs in the construction business, that sort of thing. The kind of work often referred to as “graft”. It’s from MinskWorks, the developer of Jalopy, which absolutely makes sense. Life is as fiddly as their car mechanic sim. It’s arriving on April 30 in early access.

notes.title: Jalopy, the Eastern European road trip game, is free on the Humble Store
notes.notes:
Jalopy, the "haunting piece of Eastern Bloc nostalgia" about a road trip from Berlin to Turkey in breakdown-prone Laika 601 Deluxe, is free for the taking for the next couple of days on the Humble Store. The latest Humble giveaway marks the beginning of the store's Spring Sale Encore, which features hundreds of games back on sale for the next four days. 

The Jalopy roadtrip isn't about just driving a car: You'll have to assemble it first, and keep it running, repaired, and fueled as you trudge through a bleak, procedurally generated landscape. Our 2017 hands-on paints a grim portrait of crumbling infrastructure, loneliness, and stoic introspection:   

"When I finally reach Yugoslavia, the game shows off the coastal area—something I’ve never seen before. But the roads still feel familiar. They bend in weird and dangerous ways, while stone hills loom over them. It’s nowhere in Yugoslavia; it’s everywhere in Yugoslavia. I gaze at the sea and reflect upon my journey. Have I changed like my Laika has? Different on the inside, with only the shell still the same? The car breaks down again and I’m reminded that no, it’s still the piece of garbage it has always been." 

Not exactly the new Grid, in other words, but at the price I think we can all afford a little bit of experimentation. Jalopy is free until 10 am PT/1 pm ET on May 25, while the Humble Store Spring Sale Encore will run until the same time on May 27.

notes.title: Weird, wonderful Eastern Europe roadtrip adventure Jalopy is free on the Humble Store
notes.notes:
Developer Minskworks' Jalopy is a weird, drab, dull, wonderful experience, and if you're in the mood for a bit of an Eastern European adventure in a clapped-out old banger, you'd do well to snap it up right now, while it's free on the Humble Store.

It should be a simple enough task, really; transport your uncle from one side of the former Eastern Bloc to the other, trundling happily and uneventfully through Germany, Hungary, Yugoslavia, Bulgaria, and Turkey. Unfortunately, rather complicating the adventure is the fact that your only vehicle of choice is your beloved, but barely functional, Laika 601 Deluxe - inspired by the legendary East German Trabant.

That makes for an interesting dichotomy; on the one hand, there's the endless monotony of Jalopy's wilfully drab (usually damp) landscape, trundling leisurely by outside the window. On the other, there's the constant tension that comes from the knowledge that your trusty Laika 601 is liable to jettison important bits and collapse into a pile of rust at any moment.

notes.title: New Update Now Live - Stuttering Effect Solved
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

We have noticed a handful of reports from players saying they are experiencing what appears to be a stuttering effect in game. This looks visually like a low frame rate, however the game itself it running at a much higher frame rate.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/0b1286207e2a6b7cbc5b982b90a940ddf3201b18.jpg[/img]

This issue is caused by a change in how often the physics system updates in the game - this was changed to help optimise the game further on lower end machines, but created a stuttering effect on higher end machines because of the difference between the physics update and the frame rate on screen. 

To address this, the physics will now update much quicker in game and should remove stuttering effect.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/5b2541b23a37a7eb46a976aaab2ce490673fd29c.png[/img]

We have also given the player the ability to further adjust how often this happens with launch options.

However this will make the mouse sensitivity much greater so this may need to be adjusted by the player in game.

[h1]Setting Launch Options[/h1]

- Open your library and locate Jalopy
- Right Click on Jalopy and select "Properties"
- In the general tab, click on "Set Launch Options"
- type in -fixedTime 0.01
- This will trigger the physics at 100 times a second (100fps)

We have also adjusted the default launch options for the game.

The game no longer support opengl and DX11 also will be dropped from the default launch options as this was no longer being utilised.

In place of this you will find alternative launch options which are the following:

Play on low spec PC
Play on high spec PC

These options adjust the physics updates to optimise the game for different types of PCs. 

If you have any issues or require further support.
Please email our team at support@excalibur-games.com

Thanks,
The Jalopy Team

notes.title: The problem with building a car in Jalopy
notes.notes:
This is The Mechanic, where Alex Wiltshire invites developers to discuss the difficult journeys they ve taken to make their games. This time, Jalopy [official site].

A lot of people have made the correlation between game development being a janky mess and the car in the game being a janky mess, says Greg Pryjmachuk, the sole developer of Jalopy, a game about driving a Laika 601 Deluxe through the countries of the former Soviet bloc with your uncle. It does seem quite apt.

But he s definitely being a little hard on himself. Jalopy is a game he never intended to be as big as it s become, a project he started to escape from mainstream development. A couple of weeks back, after two years in Early Access, it finally reached its official launch, and with it has come a slew of negative reviews and angry forum threads born of a weight of expectation that Jalopy s rattling old chassis was never really designed to live up to. notes.title: Road trip simulator Jalopy reaches full release next week
notes.notes:
Jalopy is a lovely road trip simulator that wheels players around the territories of the former Eastern Bloc. It's been in Early Access since April 2016, and has now set March 28, this Wednesday, for full release. 

When I first discovered former Formula 1 developer Greg Pryjmachuk was partly responsible for Jalopy, I was intrigued. Driving an East German Trabbie-aping Laika 601 Deluxe is a far cry from high-velocity F1 cars, and while I loved my time with it I'm not sure I properly understood it. 

Miodrag Kovachevic's 2017 Now Playing, on the other hand, is a wonderful example of someone who does. As explained in the article's intro, Miodrag grew up in '90s Yugoslavia, an Eastern European country that no longer exists. They speak about their family's Yugo—"a metal box with wheels that was the embodiment of cheap communist cars"—which, despite lasting 27 years, appears to mirror the game's Laika 601 Deluxe.  

Miodrag's insights inspired me to return to Jalopy, which I then found more enjoyable than before. You should absolutely read the piece in its entirety, but I've pulled out a couple of paragraphs below: 

As I drive through procedural ’90s Germany, I don’t recognise any of the environments, but I still feel a sense of nostalgia. My car is slow and the roads are barren, without a single billboard in sight. The radio plays songs that sound like Eastern Europe in the ’90s, (or Western Europe in the ’60s, depending on your perspective). A few infant ’90s tracks tentatively edge themselves in, not yet knowing whether they’re electro or industrial...

When I finally reach Yugoslavia, the game shows off the coastal area—something I’ve never seen before. But the roads still feel familiar. They bend in weird and dangerous ways, while stone hills loom over them. It’s nowhere in Yugoslavia; it’s everywhere in Yugoslavia. I gaze at the sea and reflect upon my journey. Have I changed like my Laika has? Different on the inside, with only the shell still the same? The car breaks down again and I’m reminded that no, it’s still the piece of garbage it has always been. 

Jalopy will launch in full on March 28, and will be subject to a limited-time 40 percent launch discount on Steam. It'll support 19 different languages, too—check out that list full over here.

notes.title: Jalopy Leaves Early Access On 28th March 2018
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Today we are sharing some important news on Jalopy: version 1.0 will drop on 28th March 2018, marking the end of the Early Access period.

Jalopy has been in development for over three years now, and debuted in Early Access nearly two years ago. Greg has been the sole developer of the project, but along the way we’ve had others help us, including Jeremy, who scored the fantastic soundtrack.

We would like to thank everyone who has purchased the game so far and has helped to support the game’s development for the past two years. We hope that you have enjoyed watching the game grow and have loved being a part of this road-trip. 

Jalopy’s full launch on 28th March will also see the debut of full translation into 18 different languages. Thanks to the wonderful community translation project, 28th March will see Jalopy available fully translated into the following languages:

English
French
German
Italian
Spanish
Japanese
Korean
Russian
Brazilian Portuguese
Turkish
Hungarian
Chinese (Simplified)
Dutch
Norwegian
Finnish
Polish
Slovakian
Romanian
Croatian

At the beginning of Jalopy’s life, and throughout the Early Access period, a number of questions and answers have been present on Jalopy’s Steam store page – and now that we have almost reached the end of Early Access it feels right to revisit those questions. 

 [h1]Why Early Access?[/h1]
“The instant feedback from Steam players allows us to reshuffle our priorities during development to make an even better game. During the Early Access period the game will most certainly contain a selection of bugs, glitches, and issues that can impact a traditional game experience. If you do buy the game and come across something odd, please tell us in the forums.”

Jalopy has contained many bugs and issues throughout the development period - we’re still ironing out just a few, but believe that the game breaking issues are gone (do let us know if you come across any game breaking issues, though!).

Most notably we saw the uncle removed from the game for a period and then eventually brought him back after we fixed some of the issues that were present because of his role in the game. He has since returned, new and improved, with a stronger emphasis on the narrative of Jalopy and has given the game an ending for players.

[h1]Approximately how long will this game be in Early Access?[/h1]
“We are looking to release the full game towards the end of 2017.”
We are a little late on this estimation. It took a little longer for us to handle the localisation than we expected. Jalopy will launch as a full game on 28th March 2018.

[h1]How is the full version planned to differ from the Early Access version?[/h1]
“In Early Access you will be able to drive, explore and trade throughout Germany & the CSFR. Already, the player can make changes to their vehicle with millions of combinations available to affect vehicle performance. As we progress through Early Access we plan to let the player drive through 1990’s renditions of Hungary, Yugoslavia, Bulgaria and Turkey. Early Access will be an insight into the core mechanics of Jalopy and from here we plan to build around this core with feedback from the community.”

At launch we began with just the countries of Germany and CSFR. We have since added all promised countries including Hungary, Yugoslavia, Bulgaria and Turkey. During development we worked on improving the vehicle handling and have added new unlocks to the vehicle like an internal dashboard display, paint and a few other upgrades to the car itself. We also introduced the scrapyard, which allows players to scavenge for goods if they can figure out how to unlock the gate. Jeremy also created new pieces of music for each country as they released.

[h1]What is the current state of the Early Access version?[/h1]
“The game contains all final countries planned for the final game. Players can upgrade their car, purchase new components, scavenge for items and drive back to the starting area once they reach the final destination.”

This section was adjusted throughout development in order to reflect the current status of the game. 

[h1]Will the game be priced differently during and after Early Access?[/h1]
“The price may increase with significant content updates. We will let everyone know if the price is expected to rise before it increases.”

The game did increase in price slightly during development and we communicated the increase with players. With the announcement of the last price increase, we alerted players that this was the final time the price would increase.

[h1]How are you planning on involving the Community in your development process?[/h1]
“Once we get into Early Access we’re going to be looking at the most important features within the first week or two of release. From here we will create a development roadmap so that everyone can visualise where the game is heading and can get involved. Of course, do say hi to us in the Steam forums and let us know your thoughts on the game.”

This may have changed a little since the beginning of Early Access. We responded to several bugs and issues, the largest of which was the uncle causing crashes. Our development roadmap was predominately based around the addition of countries. Greg had a Tumblr blog where he would answer questions directly and share progress and concerns during development. We often had pages of change logs for each update and worked on making these updates exciting events. We additionally set the Beta Branch accessible to all players during some testing phases so players would see advance builds before they were made public. This assisted in locating important issues as we prepared for builds to go public.

[h1]What We Could Not Deliver[/h1]
Now this is an interesting but particularly difficult subject to discuss. However, I feel it’s important to speak about the elements which we were unable to achieve, despite us discussing them in the past or having hopes that these would eventually see the light of day.

[b]Steering Wheel Support[/b]
We managed to get the game running well on one type of steering wheel. We did release a build on Steam with the following disclaimer on 20th September 2017:

“The latest build adds steering wheel support, but there is a massive disclaimer we need to mention. We have been performing some tests internally and there are still issues with this. There are still many wheels that are not yet functioning correctly and is something that is being looked at. If you experience non-functioning pedals, or the view rotates without any input, we highly recommend that you continue to use a mouse and keyboard or a game pad instead.“

There were a few questions in the forum asking about steering wheel support over time, and I replied personally to some and said that if they wanted to buy the game because of steering wheel support, I highly recommend that they wait until a later date.

Unfortunately, we have been unable to make any progress on this area and there will be no steering wheel support for Jalopy. It is disappointing, and something we hoped would be in the game, but we were unable to truly support it and get it working for everyone.

[b]Mac Support[/b]
We were intending to support Mac early on in development – however, as we were looking towards a 1.0 release, we came across some issues that would make the transition from Windows to Mac much more difficult. In February, I posted the following in response to a thread asking for Mac support.

“Unfortunately porting to Mac would require the game to be rewritten in xcode and new shaders would need to be created. We are also suffering from ram issues due to the version of Unity we're running (Unity 4.6). So it seems like it will be very unlikely for a Mac version to happen.”

A little time has passed since that post, and unfortunately Mac support is not going to be possible for Jalopy, due to issues with the game engine.

So, there we go! Right now, we’re working on implementing translations and fixing any game-breaking bugs for the final release. If you do spot any bugs and can reproduce it 100%, send us over the details of what happens and how to reproduce it - we will look towards addressing any such issues. 

We will likely have a launch discount for Jalopy on the 28th of March, so stay tuned for further information over the next couple of weeks.

Thank you once again for joining us on this Jalopy journey. It’s been a road trip like no other.

notes.title: The Uncle Update Is Live!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/1d9c263a4c0b04079320a67341d70327fe1f79ee.jpg[/img]

Hello Everyone,

Jalopy receives a pretty major update today which brings back the Uncle and introduces a narrative element to the game.  I’ll go through some of the larger points included in this update, but there will of course be a large change log at the end of this post for you to read in more detail.

[h1]The Uncle Is Back[/h1]
Your second travelling companion (of course, after the Laika 601 Deluxe) asks you to transport him to Turkey. Along the way, he’ll share information of the local area, warn you when your bonnet is open and may help you if you have begun running a bit low on funds. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/0b1286207e2a6b7cbc5b982b90a940ddf3201b18.jpg[/img]

There’s always been a divide of opinion on the uncle, some love him and his dimension shifting jacket, while others have a hatred that matches that of standing bare foot on a Lego piece. So with that in mind, once you complete the tutorial and complete your first route. When you load up the game you will be given the option to either have him accompany you on your journey or leave him behind. 

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/81f7089bd8b780ec2f165b7afd29e9e3e4c2378a.jpg[/img]

Uncle may still be a little buggy. But do let us know if he begins to misbehave!
Of course, the narrative elements introduced via the uncle is something that you should discover yourself. We hope you enjoy the story!

[h1]Steering Wheel Support[/h1]
The latest build adds steering wheel support, but there is a massive disclaimer we need to mention. We have been performing some tests internally and there are still issues with this. There are still many wheels that are not yet functioning correctly and is something that is being looked at.  If you experience non-functioning pedals, or the view rotates without any input, we highly recommend that you continue to use a mouse and keyboard or a game pad instead. 

[h1]Statistics[/h1]
If you’ve ever wanted to know how many footsteps you’ve taken, how many tyres you’ve popped and what your top speed is, you’re in luck! The statistics screen now tracks many of your actions while playing. I’ll be personally curious to see who will be able to reach the highest speed in their Laika 601 Deluxe.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/8a106bb2b857120d2f546c1d87c1dddcc69c98d5.jpg[/img]

[h1]Achievements[/h1]
Achievements have been added! There are some particularly easy achievements that ca n be obtained within minutes, but then there’s some tough ones for those staying for the long haul. Good luck everyone!

[h1]Trabant Car Challenge with Hat Films[/h1]
And finally, we have been working with Hat Films to create a three part series where the guys from Hat films drive a couple of Trabants. The first episode is live now, you can watch it below:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nEOgev7e_Vw

So, there we go! This update helps to fill a narrative shaped hole which was in Jalopy. Of course, there are a few dozen fixes for some issues as well. If you experience any issues, do let us know in the forums! Thankyou everyone for the support and patience as we’ve been working on this update.

If you'd like to read the full change logs click the link below:

[url=https://www.excalibur-publishing.com/blogs/news/jalopy-uncle-update] Change Log[/url]

notes.title: Jalopy - Price Increase Announcement
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

We must welcome everyone who has joined us over the last several days during the Steam summer sale. I'd also like to give a thank you to those who have been helping out our new players by answering questions in the forum.

I wanted to let everyone know that we are planning to increase the price for Jalopy slightly shortly after the Steam Summer sale. This will be the final price of the game and there will be no more price increases after this... This also means there will be no price increase for the games full game launch. 

Of course, if you bought the game already, you of course don't need to pay any extra! I didn't think I would need to mention this but I believe I will still get this question via email a few times :)

There are several reasons to initiate a price increase, but one of the biggest reasons is to maximize the games presence when it does launch as a full game. It's all very boring behind the scenes strategy to help market the game  and is part of the less interesting side of game development, but I hope that many of you understand as it will allow us to reach more players and hope to sustain a good future for us even after the games full release.

As promised in the Early Access questions, I said that I would let everyone know if a price increase was planned to happen. It's not an easy job to value and price your game (in fact this is the most difficult thing to do in order to value the worth of something you have worked on!).

Thank you to everyone who has bought the game so far and helped support us. We hope that you've enjoyed the game so far and continue to support us by leaving questions and engaging in the forums.

Now, regarding the actual development!

Right now Greg is working on bringing back the Uncle, but also looking at Steering Wheel Support as well. Sorry this post isn't very development heavy, it's more of an admin related post. We''ll get to the more exciting side of Games development very soon and show off new things within the next few weeks!

[h1]Update 7th July 2017:[/h1]
The price Increase is now live.

notes.title: Bulgaria Update Out Now! Tyres, New Cashier System, New Music and 33% off
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/4a3d7dfc04bdb5cbceb72f10b66adbdb624a55b7.png[/img]
Hello everyone,

Jalopy has just received a brand new update which brings with it some adjustments to tyre wear, new tyre types, more music tracks Bulgaria to explore and a selection of other changes and fixes. For just a brief look at some of the changes, you can watch the trailer for the Bulgaria route here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PNqvW88vtwE
Those of you who want to know more about the changes, I’ll go into a lttle more detail below:

[h1]New Tyre System[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/12f9d596ee0afc95d2d2c0fa7cefa25c64f384e2.png[/img]

Previously, players would need to just replace their tyres when they burst. Now, we have a selection of different conditions which affect tyre traction. If you’re driving in pouring rain, you’re going to want wet tyres, if you fancy off roading, you’re probably going to want to fit some off road tyres.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/9230625f76d801042a4a1de83af5db4ba31c1bce.png[/img]

The tyres can be purchased from petrol stations and the Autershop at the end of each route and come in several variants including soft, medium and hard compound.

Soft Compound: Tyres wear at a faster rate but have an increased level of grip
Medium Compound: Tyres wear at an average rate and have an average level of grip
Hard compound: Tyres wear at a slower rate but they have a decreased level grip

Remember, your Laika 601 Deluxe can store two tyres in the trunk, but you can hold additional tyres with the officially licensed roof rack which can be found inside Laika Dealerships.

[h1]New Music[/h1]
Jeremy has been at it again and has created two more tracks for Jalopy! 

[h1]New Cashier system[/h1]
When selling goods, you now may be alerted by the cashier that they can’t afford to buy what you are selling. When choosing a route, the cashiers on the route will spawn with a certain number of finances available to them, up to 300. We have seen some playthroughs where a lucky spawn for a crate of wine will give players a massive influx of cash which makes upgrading your car much more satisfying.

Bear in mind though, that while the cashier may not be able to afford the goods you want to sell with cash, you may be able to exchange it for any items in the shop. Make sure to place the goods you want to trade it for onto the counter first before placing the goods you want to sell.

[h1]Bulgaria[/h1]

This is the penultimate location for Jalopy. It features large off road areas, winding roads and flooded off road tracks. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/faa1c3f7709e0f99ab125cd26c56eba86a98fca5.png[/img]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/17770261/49013dca558d1459c14add32d1ecb030eebc4899.png[/img]

Greg is now at work on the Turkey route, which will be the final destination in Jalopy. Once that’s been added we will start looking at several other features including driving back home. More details will be shared in the coming weeks

To celebrate the new Bulgaria update, we have also put the game into a 33% off discount on Steam.

As always, thank you for the support, if you experience any issues, let us know in the forums or email us at support@excalibur-publishing.com
A full change Log is below

- Top speed and acceleration now capped correctly when pushing the car while engine is running

[h1]0.72[/h1]
- Fixed wet tyre grip not being used in wet weather

- straightened tyre alignment
- lowered skid audio

- Fixed shader issue with Bul_0-0_03 road
- halved skidding wear rates again
- Increased all base tyre grip levels by 10%
- Shortened map strings for Bulgaria
- Fixed collision issues for Bul_0-0_08
- Fixed stop off not spawning at Bul_0-0_06
- Fixed Bulgaria petrol station font appearing through environment

- Fixed loot spawning in abandoned cars falling through environment
- Fixed page turning issue with User Manual
- Fixed tyre spawning issue with abandoned cars
- Fixed issue with Uncle repeating tutorial dialogue when using the same car jack used in the tutorial
- after completing the tutorial - Uncle no longer repeats tyre tutorial dialogue
- Actually fixed puddles preventing players from picking items out of them
- Player no longer floats away from home storage if using it while holding items 
- Fixed wallet floating away in Home Storage
- Fixed issue with moving items from home or crate inventories shaking the car
- Fixed issue with items placed in crates or home inventories adding weight to the car
- Fixed incorrect value used to calculate component weights when stored in the rear of the car
- Car's Trunk / Boot weight now affects rear grip as well as rear tyre wear
- Overall car weight now affects all tyre grip, the heavier the car the more traction it will have (car weight can be viewed in the user manual) 
- Fixed 0 pricing issue caused by economy generation

[h1]0.644[/h1]
- Can no longer drop tyre iron while removing tyres, which was causing tyre iron to get locked in hands unusable
- Fixed issue with tyre iron bolt not unhighlighting when hovering over the tyres - will make it much clearer when removing tyres
- Fixed red tube carburetor having constant spanner UI appear
- Fixed being able to drop the car jack while loosening wheel bolts
- Fixed potholes and puddles appearing sideways over railroads in CSFR
- Fixed AI pileup issue in Hungary
- Fixed electrical audio hum not playing near Petrol Station signage

[h1]0.645[/h1]
- Fixed weird issues caused by economy State & hub Layout not deleting during new game
- Stealing & saving now removes all home storage and all items stored in them. CRIME DOES NOT PAY.
- Lowered joypad dead zone from 0.5 to 0.1
- Further increased tyre grip levels and additional 20%

[h1]0.6451[/h1]
- Reverted input sensitivity changes

[h1]0.6452[/h1]
-implemented saving and loading of tyres
-tyres will not return to axle when taking other tyres out of the boot below!

notes.title: Jalopy Build 06203 Now Live (Rolling And Pushing)
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, 

The latest build of Jalopy (Build 06203) is now live. This build contains some slight improvements to the AI performance but also a couple of new features. 

The images below are from the [url=https://twitter.com/JalopyGame]@JalopyGame[/url] twitter account. Make sure to follow as Greg posts a few teaser images and details on this account.

If you've somehow managed to topple your car over into a full roll, you'll now be able to salvage the car by rolling it back into the upright position. Simply click on the cars frame and you'll attempt to roll it back over.

[img]http://imgur.com/gHoQoD3.gif[/img]

Those who became stranded due to running out of fuel or neglecting general maintenance used to have to walk to the nearest petrol station. While you'll still need to try and get to the petrol station, at least you can now bring the car with you. Hop out of the car, click and hold on the steering wheel and push!

[img]http://imgur.com/6AxdOnT.gif[/img]

We noticed in the last build that some users are experiencing FPS drops. If this build has not increased the FPS for you, please do the following:

[list][*]Go into the options menu and decrease the AI density
[*]If this doesn't work, contact us at support@excalibur-publishing.com with your dxdiag and details on estimated frame rates and where you experience any drops[/list]

We'll do our very best to help anyone who contacts us on this, so any further info would allow us to work towards any fixes.

[h1]Changelog 06203[/h1]
[*]Doubled timestep to improve physics performance (physics now ticks at 100fps rather than 200fps) 
[*]Can now roll the car by clicking on the frame 
[*]Can now push the car by clicking and holding on the steering wheel while outside of the drivers seat 
[*]Cleaned up the car jack so it doesn't appear floating anymore[/list

notes.title: Yugoslavia update public beta now live
notes.notes:
Jalopy is still in Early Access but has been subject to updates and new territories almost constantly since launch and we are now nearing the next major update to include the country once known as Yugoslavia.  

Take a drive along the coastline of what is now known as Croatia along winding roads, discover abandoned lighthouses, scavenge deserted beaches and build your bank balance trading a whole new raft of territory specific goods.  

There are also three new major components to enable the player to upgrade their car.  
•	The Light Rack will give better illumination for improved viewing
•	Digital Dash Display will keep you informed about your cars performance
•	A Tool Rack can be installed to save space in the rear of the car

Players with Xbox 360 controllers can now rejoice, as support for this controller has now been added with plans to support more input devices in the future.

There's also an array of graphical improvements to the game including a rebuilt car dashboard which makes each component much more apparent. The rear and side view mirrors now function as in a real car and support for Anti-Aliasing has also made its way into the game. 

Considerable time has been spent refining some smaller elements of the visual style of the game. For example black shades are now much less dense and with a hint of purple allowing for better contrast on darker monitors.  Night time is less punishingly dark than in previous versions of the game.

Thanks to much community feedback there has been a long list of bug fixes and with loads of surprises to be found in this next update. You can now honk the horn of your Laika to warn oncoming traffic. Save a huge amount of components with the home storage system, lose money on components as their value adjusts dynamically related to their condition, and much more. We really think the wait for this one will have been worth it. 

We fully expect this new update to be added to the Jalopy build on Steam within the next couple of weeks but for those gamers who have already purchased Jalopy, they can access the public beta of the new content by following the steps below. 
  
1.	Open Steam on your PC and go to your library
2.	Right click on Jalopy and then click on Properties
3.	Select the BETAS tab and then in the dropdown menu select public_beta
4.	Once selected, Steam should automatically start downloading the beta content
5.	To opt-out of the beta repeat steps 1- 3 but select NONE in the drop down box

A full list of changes will follow shortly, but for the early birds we won't spoil any surprises just yet.

notes.title: The Perfect Roadtrip Game
notes.notes:
I’ve played a few games about roadtrips recently. It wasn’t intentional, though I do love the idea of games about journeys, they all just happened to land in my lap at the same time. First up was Overland, a turn-based tactical post-apocalyptic game about travelling across a bug-infested America. Then there was The Crew, in which I competed with Brendan in a race. That also took me across the US. If you’d rather escape the US, check out the excellent Death Road to Canada, which is funny, short and sweet…with lots of guts and headshots.

And there’s Jalopy, a game about car maintenance and travelling across the former Eastern bloc. Finally, I spun the Wheels of Aurelia, the most interesting of the three in many ways. That’s a game about the conversations you have with people as you drive, rather than the driving itself.

notes.notes:

We are looking forward to seeing players share their screenshots as they explore. However, the new route is not the only addition, there are a variety of features that have been added to compliment the Hungary update.

[h1]Spray Paints[/h1]
The spray can is our first new addition. You will be able to purchase these from your Laika Dealership. However they can only stock a limited number of supplies so you’ll need to visit the shop often to make sure they have the colour you want.

If you have a red coat of paint on your Laika 601 Deluxe, you can spray a blue paint over it to mix the two colours and create a purple variant. Experimenting with colour mixing allows you to create some great personal designs.

[img]http://i.giphy.com/26gJzZNavf1q1GRsA.gif[/img]

You’ll also be able to spray paint the interior of your Laika 601 Deluxe

[img]http://i.giphy.com/l0HlIjWrpq7RXYGqs.gif[/img]

For those looking for a stylistic sheen, then you are going to want to slap some metallic paint on your Laika 601 Deluxe. 

[img]http://i.giphy.com/3o6ZsZr73dfn3Zv50Q.gif[/img]

And finally, a special addition to the spray paint are the Decal boxes. The decal boxes allow for more customisation options for your Laika 601 Deluxe and come in several variants. From a classic checkerboard roof to flames.
 
[img]http://i.giphy.com/3o6ZtppDDHYrJUYc8w.gif[/img]

The decal system is more than likely to be expanded upon throughout Early Access. Do let us know what kind of decals you would like to have in the comments below.

[img]http://i.giphy.com/3o6Ztn99xqrAofOgVi.gif[/img]

[h1]Country branded items[/h1]

[img]http://i.giphy.com/l0HlwvtINimhFsIpO.gif[/img]

[h1]New spawning system for abandoned cars[/h1]
Abandoned cars now spawn more dynamically in the world. Eagle eyed drivers will need to keep an eye out for these as they can hold some valuable engine parts or replacement wheels.

[h1]The scrapyard[/h1]
When selecting a route, you may come across a scrapyard. If you have the tools, you can fix the mechanism at the front of the gate and enter the scrap yard to search for engine parts. Be cautious as using your own engine parts is a big risk of getting yourself stranded… But don’t you want to know what’s inside!?

[img]http://i.giphy.com/l0Hlw6HaXMv0FYA00.gif[/img]

[h1]New main menu background[/h1]
The games menu now remembers where you have last saved and will create a background image to match the next area.

[h1]New music[/h1]
Jeremy has produced some excellent new tracks for Jalopy. You will be able to listen to them in the main menu or even in game on the radio. We hope you enjoy them and hope that as the game continues to grow, Jeremy will continue to provide some new music for the game. 

You can head over to Jeremy’s website below:

https://jeremywarmsley.wordpress.com/music/

[h1]Weight limit in the manual[/h1]
The car manual has gone through a small overhaul. Various texture issues have been addressed and we’ve added some more functionality. Towards the back end of the manual you can check the weight limit of your car.

[img]http://i.giphy.com/3o6Zt5W3p2Ae2iZVQc.gif[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TL-2VNX8xsk

We hope you enjoy exploring Hungary, we will be keeping an eye in the forums for any bugs or issues so please do let us know if you experience anything out of the ordinary. We hope you enjoy the update, the next major update planned is for the country of Yugoslavia.

- Added Hungary
- Added Decals
- Added Paint Cans
- Added Scrapyards
- Added Abandoned Car Spawning
- Additional Music from Jeremy
- Added Storage page to manual
- Added Country Specific Goods
- Added Odometer
- Added item in the back seat 
- Petrol stations now spawn based upon country

[b]MINOR[/b]
- Changed daytime ambient audio
- Various oil Mix issues fixed
- Various Battery issues fixed
- Sleep texts fixes
- Car Tilting fixed
- Decals being deleted fixed
- Fixed Newspapers not displaying correct information
- Desktop Icon added
- Menu Music updated
- Front End Menu background now changes based on save location
- Uncle restricted from travel
- Fixed Manual flickering
- Increased Day Cycle from 15 minutes to 18
- Oil should now work and display correctly, with refueling reducing oil mix
- New Weather effects

- One of our machines had experienced some crashing when interacting with certain items. We nailed this down to directx9 on that machine. But it was working well on other machines. When launching on DirectX 11, there were no more crashes. We have added an option when loading the game to select which DirectX version you would like to launch the game in. if you experience any crashes, it might be that you have to choose a different DirectX at launch
- Black screen when changing graphical options – If this happens, alt tab out and force the game to close. The game will remember your graphical settings even if you force a close.
- Low FPS – Some users are still running the game with V Sync on and highest graphical settings. Turning V Sync off significantly decreases FPS loss at night (our machines here run at a minimum of 50FPS at night and experience upwards of 120FPS during the day).

-	Fixed several issues where battery functionality at 0% was causing components to think that they could still work (caused hazard and engine horrible sound bugs
-	Fixed passport being broken after crossing the first border
-	Fixed a lack of collisions on the Germany to CSFR border tunnels
-	Uncle  should no longer complain if the radio is too loud
-	Rain Audio should no longer continue into sunny days
-	Fixed a decal still having debug text present
-	Using the scrapyard engine no longer destroys components but instead uses 1 lt fuel, and 10% battery charge
-	Scrapyard engine gates now better displays information regarding what is wrong with the gate engine
-	No more tiny tyres on abandoned cars
-	Scrapyard items no longer mess up engine components in the car
-	Fixed some interaction issues between removing a component from its holder and placing it down too quickly
-	Fixed inventory save/load issue: Inventory wasn't clearing the recorded data for the country you purchased a tradeable good in, so when swapping that out with another item (I.e a bottle of water) it would try to assign a country ID to it and get stuck. 

If anyone has any issues, please do keep letting us know. We thank you all for getting involved in the development of Jalopy.

[h1]UPDATE  25th JULY 2016[/h1]
Hello everyone,

Jalopy patch has gone live today. We’re looking at ironing out some of the bugs that players have discovered. This may not be all, but please bear with us as we are still working on them.

This hotfix includes:
-	Fixed an issue where the roof rack caused a save and load corruption
-	Fixed an error where Save & quit, Restart and Return Home options in pause menu would not work
-	Fixed an issue with items in the inventory becoming unparented when trying to pick them up with your hands full
-	Fixed an issue with loading from motels causing a path finding loop which resulted in a performance drop
-	Fixed an issue where doors would not have bells
-	Fixed uncle talking when not in car and telling the player to put items back
-	Fixed interior rain audio still playing on the next day after rain conditions

We are still working towards fixing some of the more serious issues. So please keep checking back as we look to issue another patch this week. We thank every one of you who has helped provide reproduction steps so that we can try to locate and eliminate these issues!

notes.title: Jalopy Performance Patch
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Today we’re releasing a new update for Jalopy which introduces a few changes to performance. As you know, optimisation is something that we are planning to work on throughout development and it will take some time.

[h1]ChangeLog:[/h1]
[list][*]Flickering lights option in the option menu now works
[*]Work done towards framerate drop at night
[*]Trunks should no longer duplicate items when placing 1x2x1 items in roof rack
[*]Placing engine components into trunk should no longer make your car freak out[/list]

[h1]Adjusting graphic settings:[/h1]
We’ve noticed that V sync can cause the game to suffer from a severe FPS loss. If you are experiencing any FPS drops at night, we recommend you turning off Vsync and SSAO. Running the game on low to medium settings during this can make the game run on our machines at around 90FPS in towns during night, where on high they could drop to about 20FPS.

Do adjust your graphical options, the low poly allows for a lot more leeway on these settings and know that optimisation will continue to be an ongoing process during development.

[h1]Hungary Update[/h1]
Regarding the Hungary update, Greg is working very hard on the core generation of Hungary and will be spending more time refining new features. This will of course go into some internal testing before release and over the next few weeks we will begin to share more details on the update and what features you can look forward to seeing. Thankyou everyone for your patience!

notes.title: Build 04695: Conquering Inclines, AI Driver Improvements, Ear Drums Saved!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, in today’s update we have continued our quest to stomp out bugs! We’ve also added a few options to customize your experience while on the road.

First, we’ve been working towards the dangerous drivers who have been reversing up hills because their car lacked the momentum to travel in forward motion. Drivers can now stop on a hill and perform a true hill start by applying the handbrake, releasing and then accelerating.  A variety of other car handling fixes have been made.

Additionally, we’ve been having a chat with some of the AI drivers who have been finding it difficult to build up the courage to enter a roundabout. They have since returned to driving school in order to become more confident behind the wheel. This should mean that there are no longer large traffic jams approaching a town. 

Should there still be any AI driver issues, we’ve also added an option to decrease the density of traffic. 

Fans of having ear drums will now be able to open the game without fear of them bursting from the main menu music. While Jeremy’s music is lovely, we had to turn it down a little bit!
We’ve also nailed the issue where water tanks do not spawn when ordered from the Laika dealership. They will currently float just outside the shop, but that’s a pretty good compromise to get the feature working!

Finally we have made some work towards lighting optimisation, added an SSAO video option, fixed an issue with fuel mix load save issue, fixed an issue where abandoned cars would spawn items that they shouldn’t 

On a final note. I feel it is important to note that optimisation is an ongoing process through development, we have made some changes however it is something that will continue to be worked upon throughout the entirety of development. It will take time, but be assured we will be working on optimisation.

If you have any bugs to report, as always do let us know in the forums. Thankyou!

[b][h1]Something for the future [/h1][/b]
This is a new section, where we tell you about something that Greg is working on, but is not yet in the game. As you may know, the next major update will be the Hungary update. We don’t yet have a date for this just yet as we are focusing on bug stomping..

As part of the Hungary update, Greg has shared details on his dev blog (http://minskworks.tumblr.com/) that shares details on a new feature, the spray cans. 

Check them out below:

[img] http://66.media.tumblr.com/59d8863b67c57621c7d2cd3c1251ddb3/tumblr_o70eikTcgX1s8u2wbo2_500.gif[/img]
[img] http://66.media.tumblr.com/b238872b45d91cdc6903415f6d47e129/tumblr_o70eikTcgX1s8u2wbo3_500.gif[/img]
[img] http://66.media.tumblr.com/a4ad0a5bb9791ab2dae2fa28954da85c/tumblr_o70eikTcgX1s8u2wbo1_500.gif[/img]

On the tumblr blog Greg shares just a little more detail on the plans for the spray can:

“… I’d like to make a load of different styles that you can mix and match with. Metallic colours, gradients, florescent, all change depending on the colours you mix together. Basically, the painting works based on applying the current colour you are using to your car by how long you spray your car for. So if you want a really blue car, hold down the blue spray can on the car. If you want a darker blue, use the blue spray then add some black with the black spray can”

Once we nail down a date for the Hungary update, we’ll post more details

notes.title: Build 04692 Now Live: Save Progress After Sleeping At A Motel & Various Fixes
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, build number 04692 goes live today! The most prominent addition to this build is the ability to save and quit after sleeping at a motel, and when you continue the game you will be at the last motel you slept at.

There are a few notes to consider on this. Firstly, we have added a new selection in the pause menu titled “return home”. Pressing this will return you back to the original garage area, pressing restart will return you to where you last slept.

Additionally the game calculates the games economy on route generation, if you save in Dresden, quit and then load the game again, The Autershop in Dresden won’t have an economy and will have a closed gate... We strongly recommend you make all your shops in the Autershop before sleeping in a motel... Once you’ve crossed the border, the game will generate an economy so any petrol stations or Autershops on the route will remain open.

[h1]List of changes for 04692:[/h1]
[list][*]Can now save progress after sleeping at a motel
[*]Added a return home button in the pause menu
[*]A drop & pick up timer that creates double click issues.
[*]Fixed an issue where the Laika catalogue will steal your wallet
[*]Crate prices update when in trunk
[*]Additional inventory fixes (Large crates mostly)
[*]Fixed wine clipping issue on wooden crates.[/list]

If you spot any issues, do let us know in the Steam forums!

notes.title: Build 04691 Now Live: AI Driver Improvements, Uncle Issues Addressed And More
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

We have been overwhelmed by the amazing amount of support from the community for Jalopy.  There have been some teething issues regards to bugs, but we are in the process of stomping these out with great force. Today we’re launching our third patch with some quite noticeable improvements.

The first of which is the refinement of AI drivers. If you park with your hazards lights on, they will now stop for the player. This means that the player will no longer see their car rammed by a selection of impatient drivers! Check out the video below to see the new AI details in action

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_amRK_NKxiw

We have also made some fixes towards not being able to store items in your trunk, if you are still having issues, it might mean that you will need to start a new save or delete the inventory save file in the save data.  

This can be found in: C:\Users\Username\AppData\LocalLow\MinskWorks\Jalopy

Gas cans can now be refilled, but you will have to pay for the fuel!

We have for now removed the Uncle repair and fuel tutorials, this is because they were causing some issues and causing the uncle to lock up users from interacting with objects or the uncle getting stuck outside the car.

[h1]04691 ChangeLog[/h1]
[list][*]Improved AI behaviour, other cars now stop instead of giving poor Uncle terrible whiplash
[*]Work done on Trunk space (players may need to start a new game or delete the inventory save data if there are still issues)
[*]Gas cans can now be refilled
[*]Market gate should be fixced and work as expected
[*]Uncle tutorials for fuel and repairing have been disabled due to causing some issues.[/list]
If any issues arise with this new patch, do let us new and we will look to address them!

I would also like to take some time to thank everyone who has been helping other members of the community with any issues or game tips. The community forums have been moving very fast and I am very grateful that there is already a great engagement and community around to help. Thank you!

notes.title: Jalopy Out Now In Early Access
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Jalopy has now released into Early Access! We are overwhelmed by the massive amount of support the community has given us, from preordering to offering suggestions and generally showing as much enthusiasm for the game as we have. Thankyou!

Now, Jalopy is at a stage where it is considered an Early Alpha, I feel we do have to stress that there will be bugs, there will be some features not fully implemented and that the game will continue to grow and improve over time. Choosing to purchase now allows us to continue improve the game and lets you get involved in the development process. 

So if you’re not prepared for a few issues, we strongly recommend that you wait to buy the game until it reaches a stage that you wish to invest. Those who want to join us now to report bugs and get involved in the process we welcome you to Jalopy!

We have been spending a few weeks eliminating some rather nasty bugs, but we have also eliminated some humorous issues. I felt it would be interesting to actually share a couple of the interesting bugs that we eliminated over the past week.

[b]Floating Uncle[/b]
So majestic, the uncle is a master of levitation. Or merely he has hijacked Wonder Woman’s invisible plane. Whatever the case, it was not working as intended and the uncle himself was fully aware of the bug!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/5mq0NXA.jpg[/img]

[b]Unlimited boxes[/b]
The trunk of the Laika 601 deluxe is used to transport goods which the player can sell. More often than not, decisions will need to be made regarding which goods to take on your journey.  In one circumstance the boxes in the trunk would multiply up to 18 times, providing a wealth of items to sell, completely breaking the economy!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5_OK910XHvo

These, along with many other bugs have been eliminated. If you want to track the current issues and follow our bug fixing procedure, you can even do so by visiting the following link:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MVeDYrKk1M8GAd8w4yM_yonOon49WLQIpOXyx-Y0G-Y/edit?usp=sharing

Only Excalibur and Minskworks can edit this document, but if you are interested in reporting an issue, you can use this document to see if a bug you want to report is already present in the form.

So that’s it, the game is out now, and we hope many of you will join us to help us make a great game over the coming months. If you have any questions, do get in touch with us in the forums if you have any questions.

notes.title: JALOPY LAUNCHES THIS WEEK
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/AP9nadE.jpg[/img]

Hello everyone, it will not be long now before Jalopy releases into Early Access. On the 22nd of April, the game will unlock for players. We have been taking notes on the suggestions of players and have created an internal suggestions and QA list. Very shortly we will begin work on a template of sorts that will provide details on the development roadmap.

Jalopy is for all intents and purposes considered a Pre Alpha during the first stage of Early Access. What does this mean? Well, let’s try and share our thoughts on what the definition of pre alpha means:

[list][*]A time in development where the game is not yet feature complete 
[*]At a stage where suggestions and thoughts can still shape the core gameplay 
[*]Particularly large bugs will still be present, perhaps some that may prevent progress
[*]The game will not be optimised fully[/list]

There will be bugs, there will be some features not yet implemented and maybe the game will not run well on certain PC configurations. We believe the game to still be enjoyable, but it is vital that we let you know the current state of the game so that you can make an informed purchase decision. 

If you do plan to support us, thank you! We value all feedback and if you can help stomp out some bugs by reporting them on the forums (perhaps with screenshots and video) that will really help.

So, that’s it for now! We hope that many of you will be looking forward to driving the Laika 601 Deluxe when the game launches later this week.

notes.title: A Small Delay To The Release Date
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

As you may be aware, the date of Jalopy has gone back by about one week to the 22nd of April. There are a couple of reasons for this and I'll happily share details on what we need to work on and why this decision has been made.

Firstly, we came across a rather nasty bug that we have seen some players experience but it had been quite difficult for us to reproduce. This bug caused the game to not display text. One of the problems with this bug is that it seems to affect a number of players in countries outside of the UK. Development is based in England, so we had not come across this issue and were only made aware of it recently. 

As you can expect, this nasty bug will cause quite a lot of issues and it is vital that we try to eliminate this before it is released. We are working very hard to stomp this out and hope we can fix it very soon. While we are hoping to fix this bug as soon as possible, we felt an extra week of development may also give us just a little bit more time to polish up the Early Access release too. 

We know there are a lot of you who are looking forward to the game, a delay is a tough decision we had to make but it is vital that we release the best game we can at launch. While the game will be in Pre-Alpha on release and we admit it will still contain a selection of bugs, issues and unfinished features. Development will thrive on the recommendations of our players, so we need to make sure that everyone can enjoy the game when they boot it up.

Jalopy will release very soon! And we really cannot wait for you all to play it.

notes.title: Jalopy Launches in Two Weeks - Route Generation
notes.notes:
Jalopy is just two weeks away from its Early Access launch. Developer Greg Pryjmachuk is working hard on getting the game ready for release and has shared some details on the way Jalopy handles route generation.

While we could go into more detail, part of the magic is eliminated when you begin to talk numbers. Players sharing their best trips on YouTube and taking screenshots to show landmarks is one of the key elements of the game and we are looking forward to seeing player’s first experience with the game on the 14th of April.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/HikQyvA.jpg[/img]

The driver’s side door is home to the map. From here you can choose a destination and a route. Upon selection, the game will then generate a route for you to drive. The only knowledge you have before selecting a route is whether there is a gas station mid-way, the distance of the route and which weather conditions you’d likely encounter.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/fJggT1b.jpg[/img]

On generation, factors will be decided by the game including AI placement, road conditions, package generation and building placement. Towns will also have some elements generated but will always contain a motel for you to sleep until morning, a Laika dealership to purchase new parts and a market where you will be able to sell the items you scavenged on your journey.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/y67I7eU.jpg[/img]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/XPLQdO3.jpg[/img]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/aYiRkP9.jpg[/img]

Other elements will be generated including which banned goods or low profit items are selected for the next state of countries economy. More details over on the devblog site at: http://minskworks.tumblr.com/post/141831182790/how-to-know-if-something-you-are-trying-to-take

Jalopy releases in Early Access on the 14th of April.

notes.title: Jalopy FAQ [Updated 26th of April 2016]
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! 

As we are a few weeks away from launch, we thought that we would update the Announcement page to include an FAQ!  I'll of course be updating this and the FAQ in the forums as more players ask question

[h1]When will the game launch?[/h1]
It is out now!

[h1]Can I buy direct?[/h1]
Yes, if you'd like you can purchase directly from the Excalibur Website at: http://www.excalibur-publishing.com/products/jalopy-early-access-pre-order

Ignore the preorder in the URL, we will update that soon. you will get the game sent immediately to your email inbox

[h1]How many components can we edit in the game?[/h1]
The vehicle currently has seven major engine components that can affect vehicle performance. More details on each of the engine parts are below:

[img]http://i.imgur.com/0X8Hc5C.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/1dA0VvS.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/SGwM241.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/QJz9HXh.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/gIiq2gH.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/CU4omPX.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/ZMQtdKK.png[/img]

[h1]What is currently playable in the game during Early Access[/h1]
Currently the player is able to free drive across two regions, Germany and the CSFR. Routes will be generated on selection of a destination and these will be picked from a selection of what we could call tile sets. so maybe you'll have an obstacle in one route, while another time you won't, maybe there will be a bridge, maybe you'll have an off road area to explore.

Players will be able to scavenge for items while on the road and sell these to gas stations and shops. This money can be used to upgrade your car by purchasing new car parts at the Laika garage. But the core experience is experienced from driving from destination to destination, making sure that all of the parts in your car maintained and replacing car parts for a more efficient and powerful car.

[h1]Where does the music on the radio come from?[/h1]
The Jalopy OST is by Jeremy Warmsley and can be heard in full at http://jeremywarmsley.tumblr.com/post/143316540114/so-heres-my-first-ever-videogame-soundtrack

[h1]Wheel/ Controller support?[/h1]
We are planning to work on this. Right now we are refining mechanics with mouse and keyboard support. But we are intending to feature support for both in the future.

[h1]Will there be online Multiplayer?[/h1]
The game is designed as a core single player experience where the player needs to manage the core components of the car which will damage and wear over time. We have no plans to introduce multiplayer and want to truly make a great single player game.

[h1]What formats are supported[/h1]
At Early Access launch the game will feature only PC support, but a MAC version is planned to release later.

[h1]How does saving work?[/h1]
Currently, the game saves certain details including engine components, durability, money and items in your trunk. The game does not currently save at a motel, though we are looking into that. There are elements of roguelike to the game, where each time you restart you have a chance at improving your car even further.

[h1]How can I make suggestions?[/h1]
We have a special suggestions board in the Steam forums.  Clear heading titles for your post really help us when we check out the forums and makes it easier for us to locate new and exciting ideas!

[h1]Bugs?[/h1]
Yes, there are bugs. We do consider this game to be pre alpha and understand that some things are not yet implemented, some things are not working correctly and there are a few bugs in the game. We are working on these daily.

If you want to submit a bug report, visit our bugs forum in the steam forums. You can also track a list of known bugs in the following QA document:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MVeDYrKk1M8GAd8w4yM_yonOon49WLQIpOXyx-Y0G-Y/edit?usp=sharing

[h1]What languages will be supported?[/h1]
We are focusing on the core game play at the launch of Early Access, this means English will be the priority language. However we will be looking to quickly support German, French, Italian, Spanish and Russian during Early Access. We hope to include even further support for languages!

We will be looking to localize some text files shortly after the launch of Early Access. If you want to be involved and help us localize the game into your language, do get in touch at support@excalibur-publishing.com.  

If you have any more questions, let us know in the forum and I'll of course update this post!
